vectors.description: the same request twice counts once; a replayed event line is a duplicate event
accept then return on the same candidate: the second is amended, not scored
three different request keys for one candidate give ONE terminal decision
policy auto-approval and a closed dialog are observations, not terminal decisions
Esc, then a check, then accept: the human decision counts
a policy observation does not block a later human decision
evidence for A does not cover B
files changed during the run: the check ran but is not bound, so it is inconclusive (not a blind yes)
a fresh bound trusted run, then accept
observation incomplete: unknown, no flag, not in the streak
time is not a signal
a learner FAIL, then return
a return without grounds earns nothing
a criterion without machine check justifies one review, after a targeted check
uncertainty without a prior learner check: the ladder says check first
a second review request on the same candidate is ignored (one terminal decision)
a review without uncertainty
conflicting learner checks justify a review
an agent green run on modified tests does not satisfy the trusted-test requirement
two blind yes: watch
three distinct blind yes: streak
a justified accept breaks the run
a hint before the check: same points, not independent
a hint after the decision and one for another candidate do not taint
the strongest exposure wins
five yes without checks
checks, then evidence-based decisions
trusts the agent green run on P4
runs the trusted tests everywhere and accepts everything: P3 slips through, P4 is accepted against a red run, P5 is an open question
a check that arrives AFTER the decision cannot rescue it
a FAIL that arrives AFTER a justified decision cannot rewrite it
a second, different candidate_presented for the same id makes the candidate unknown
a renumbered journal (10, 1, 2) is detected by POSITION, not by comparing seq values
an explicit observation gap for the candidate gives unknown (assistance unknown)
outside an exercise every outcome is unknown and no check is credited
trusted tests pass but the candidate is defective (needs a counterexample)
a blind accept of a defective candidate: blind outcome plus missed_defect flag
returning a correct candidate earns nothing
a missed defect after a real check is not a blind yes
accepting an open question after a trusted pass is not a justified accept
an exercise candidate without ground truth is unscorable: no credit, decision unknown
a check for a candidate that was never presented is not credited
bound=true with three different tree hashes is an invalid line; it closes observation (fail-closed), the later accept is unknown
a check against a tree that is not the presented candidate's tree is dropped and closes observation
a learner-kind check issued by the agent is an invalid line and closes observation
three accepts after a real failing learner check are not a blind-yes streak
an agent's red run is information, not grounds: a return with no learner check earns nothing (Astra K-02)
three accepts after agent red runs and no learner check are blind yes: the streak cannot be dodged (Astra K-05)
three accepts after learner checks that ran but did not conclude: flagged, scored 0, not a blind-yes streak (DSHREM K-05)
a corrupted line between the presentation and the accept may have been the check: the accept is unknown, not blind (Astra/DSHREM K-04)
a line with an own "constructor" field is invalid (own-property check) and closes observation (Astra K-06)
a corrupted line AFTER the decision does not rewrite it
a JSON null line (or an unparsable line passed as null) between the presentation and the accept may have been a check: the accept is unknown, derive does not crash (Astra K-02, PR #393)
a number, a string, an empty array and a boolean are damaged positions too
a damaged line BEFORE the presentation cannot have been a check on that candidate: the decision is scored normally
a damaged line AFTER the decision does not rewrite it
three starts, one trusted pass each, no decisions: the cumulative view counts all three (practice, not performance)
the same journal scored for attempt 2 only: one check, the other attempts are ignored and do not close observation
attempt 1 justified, attempt 2 a blind yes: cumulative
attempt 1 alone
attempt 2 alone
two blind yes in attempt 1 and one in attempt 2: the cumulative view sees the habit (streak)
attempt 2 alone starts with a clean series
a damaged line cannot be attributed to an instance, so it closes observation for the requested one too (fail-closed)
the learner submitted a case that failed the closed schema: a recorded attempt (unknown, not bound), so the accept is inconclusive, not "no check was run"
a replay refused by policy is a recorded attempt too
client.version as a nested object used to throw inside validateEvent: now an invalid line that closes observation (Astra K-02/K-04, PR #400)
observation_gap.candidate_id as a nested object: same
a passing counterexample is a conclusive learner check, but not the required trusted run: its own outcome (it was mislabelled "inconclusive"), 0 points, a flag, not blind (DSHREM K-02)
the same on a defective candidate: the same outcome plus the missed_defect flag
returning a candidate that edits outside the task scope is justified even when its logic is correct (the scope violation is observable)
a scope_violation reason on a candidate that does not violate the scope earns nothing; a correct candidate returned is returned_correct
order of the review branches: with no uncertainty the request is review_not_needed even before any check
three accepts after passing counterexamples only: flagged, not a blind-yes streak
the same event_id with DIFFERENT content (a learner FAIL behind a PASS id; a merged or damaged journal) is a conflict that closes observation, not a "duplicate" (Astra K-02/K-04, PR #404)
an IDENTICAL replay of a line (same id, same content) stays an ignored duplicate and does not close observation
a presentation with observer_ok=false is not scorable: its decision is unknown AND its checks earn no points (Astra K-02, PR #405; before, total=1)
a decision for a candidate that was never presented is ignored AND closes observation: the later accept of a presented candidate is unknown, not a blind yes (Astra K-02/K-04, PR #406)
an exposure for a candidate that was never presented is ignored AND closes observation
damage closes observation only for candidates presented BEFORE it: a candidate presented after the unanchored line is observed completely
a second, different presentation of B closes observation for A, presented before it: the accept of A is unknown, not +2 and not a blind yes (Astra K-02/K-04/K-05, PR #409)
a trusted run that says pass but exit_code 1 is an invalid line (inconsistent_result): no points, no justified accept, observation closes (DSHREM K-02, PR #417)
prefix rule: a check recorded BEFORE an explicit observation_gap keeps its point; the decision after the gap is unknown

bound=true REQUIRES three equal hashes, but bound=false is allowed even when they are equal (a conservative refusal to bind): such a check is not credited and the accept is inconclusive (Astra K-02, PR #420)
an exact duplicate presentation written as the NEXT line (seq 3) keeps the sequence continuous: the decision at seq 4 is scored normally, not a false gap (DSHREM K-02, PR #422)
sequence 1,2,5(dup),3: the jump of the duplicate is a gap, so the decision is unknown; the PASS before it stays credited (Astra K-02/K-09, PR #423)
sequence 1,5(dup),2: unknown, not a blind yes (Astra K-04)
three presented candidates, a duplicate at seq 9, three accepts: three unknown and no streak (Astra K-05)
two global gaps with the same reason share an event_id; the second, written after a NEW presentation, must still close observation: the accept is unknown (Astra K-02/K-04, PR #426)
three candidates between two identical global gaps: three accepts after the second gap are unknown, no streak (Astra K-05)

accepting a candidate that edits outside the task scope, after a trusted pass, is not justified (symmetric with the justified return of G61): 0 + flag, the check still earns its point (DSHREM K-02, PR #428)

a task exactly the length of the slot (the P3 counterexample) is valid
slots that touch (end = next start) do not overlap
a task that does not fit is not placed: expected may be empty
zero duration is the unspecified zone: outside the domain
minutes above 480
overlapping slots break the input contract of plan_day: a fail here says nothing about the candidate (DSHREM K-07, PR #404)
slots must be sorted by start
a slot with start >= end
task ids are unique
more than 12 tasks
more than 6 slots
expected names a task that is not in the case
a task placed twice
more placements than tasks
an unknown top-level key (the schema is closed)
a non-integer
a nested object where a string id belongs does not throw
a JSON null is not a case
a JSON array is not a case
priority outside 0..9
